small_guidance:
- The GEMM dominates (1024×8192×8192). Add larger tile configs tuned for this shape: `BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=64, num_warps=8, num_stages=3` and `BLOCK_M=256, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=64, num_warps=8, num_stages=3`, plus `BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=64, num_warps=8, num_stages=4`. Larger BLOCK_K (64) reduces loop iterations on K=8192.
- Since M, N, K are all multiples of 128 here, drop the boundary mask in the store and use unmasked `tl.load` in the K-loop (already unmasked — good); also set `tl.dot(..., out_dtype=tl.float32)` explicitly and consider `tf32` enabled (already on).
- For softmax with N=8192, try `num_warps=8` (instead of 16) and `num_stages=1`; a single-pass online softmax can be faster than the current two-pass when BLOCK_N==8192 fits comfortably.
large_guidance:
- Fuse softmax into the GEMM epilogue using a split-K-free, persistent row-tile design: make each program handle a full row tile (BLOCK_M rows × all N) by streaming N-tiles, keeping per-row running max/sum in registers (online softmax) so the post-GEMM tensor never round-trips to HBM. This eliminates the separate softmax kernel's full read+write of an M×N=32MB tensor.
- Alternatively, do a two-pass fused approach: pass-1 computes GEMM+bias+GELU and writes to HBM while also reducing per-row max/sum into small auxiliary tensors; pass-2 reloads and normalizes. This avoids the redundant max/sum scan in the standalone softmax.
- Consider storing weight in fp16/bf16 (cast once at init) to double effective HBM bandwidth for the GEMM; accumulate in fp32. Output stays fp32 to satisfy tolerance.
